provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: B2b family batch, consult archetype override. Two buyers on one site: employers and candidates. No fill-rate, placement or safety claims, no job board or payroll vendor names, and any agency licence stays a placeholder. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Searchable open roles by shift, location and pay as the agency posts it, apply-by-text, a bilingual application, and a note on what happens after applying
pageStructurePlus.why: Candidates decide in seconds on a phone. A staffing agency with a real jobs board gets the applicants that a flyer or a feed post loses.

pageStructurePlus.contains: For employers: roles, headcount, shift times, start date, site address, PPE and dress requirements, and a callback window from a named recruiter
pageStructurePlus.why: Plant and warehouse managers call the staffing firm that answers first. A request they can send at night gets workers on the line by morning.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Which identity and work eligibility documents to bring, safety orientation, PPE, direct deposit set-up, parking and who to ask for at the site
pageStructurePlus.why: No-shows on day one often come from confusion. A clear checklist protects the agency's reputation with the employer.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How a temp worker becomes a direct hire, the conversion terms as the agency sets them, and what the employer and worker each do
pageStructurePlus.why: Employers ask about conversion before signing. Workers ask about it before applying. One page answers both sides of the staffing deal.

pageStructurePlus.section: Timesheets and pay day for workers
pageStructurePlus.contains: How hours are submitted and approved, the pay day, pay options the agency offers, and who to call when a shift's hours look wrong
pageStructurePlus.why: Pay confusion is the top reason temp workers quit an agency. Answering it on the page keeps the bench full.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How recruiters visit a client site before sending workers, what they check, PPE responsibility, and how a worker reports a safety concern
pageStructurePlus.why: Light industrial employers and workers both want to know the agency checks the site. It answers a liability question before it is asked.

designDirections.name: Now Hiring
designDirections.bestFor: Single-office temp agencies that need applicants first and employer orders second
designDirections.headlineSample: Warehouse and light industrial jobs in {City}, apply today
designDirections.whyItFits: Citrus Morning is warm and readable on a cheap phone, which is where most candidates for temp and light industrial work apply.

designDirections.name: Two Doors
designDirections.bestFor: Staffing firms serving employers and candidates equally, with a recruiter call booking for each
designDirections.headlineSample: Staffing for {City} employers, jobs for {City} workers
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo: a dark logistics page reads as cold to job seekers. Cobalt Wire is light and credible for employers while staying friendly on a phone.

designDirections.name: Workforce Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Agencies selling multi-site light industrial staffing programmes to plants and distribution centres
designDirections.headlineSample: Light industrial staffing for {City} plants and warehouses
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo suits the employer-facing programme page: shift tables, headcount and site lists read like the ops data a plant manager uses.

openers.line: Your staffing agency's Google listing has no website, so a warehouse manager short three pickers tonight can't see what roles you fill before calling someone else.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What that warehouse manager could open instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your open jobs are Facebook posts that scroll away in a day. A candidate looking for second-shift work can't search them, and an employer can't tell you're a real staffing firm.
openers.hook: Tap the Website link or bio link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Count how many job posts you see this week.
openers.linkLine: A searchable jobs board for your agency: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing lists jobs that look months old and an application form that doesn't send. Candidates who apply and hear nothing tell their friends.
openers.hook: Open the site and check the newest job date or test the form. Note what you find.
openers.linkLine: Same staffing agency, with jobs that are current: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your recruiting site's application form needs zooming on every field. Temp work applicants tend to apply from a phone between shifts.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and try to start an application. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: An application that works on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way for a plant manager to put in a staffing order online. A form asking for roles, headcount, shift and start date would catch the requests that come in at night.
openers.hook: Check their site and listing for an employer request form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A headcount request built for employers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your hiring event flyers and team photos show a real recruiting operation, and they disappear after the event. A page that keeps them up tells candidates you hire every week.
openers.hook: Find one hiring event or team post. Name the event if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your hiring events on a page that stays: {demo-link}

openers.line: A worker's review saying your recruiter got them placed in a week and paid on time is the line the next applicant needs to see beside the jobs board.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase from a worker or an employer. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Worker and employer reviews beside the jobs: {demo-link}

openers.line: Warehouses and distribution centres ramp up for the autumn peak and start calling staffing agencies weeks before. The firms they can find online get the big orders.
openers.hook: Use from late summer through early autumn, or before a local seasonal ramp. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the peak season staffing rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: A supervisor finds out at ten at night that two forklift operators called out. If your agency's line goes to voicemail, the staffing order goes to the agency that picks up.
openers.hook: Call their number in the evening and note whether anything takes the request.
openers.linkLine: A staffing page that takes the night call-out order: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a recruiter for your own office. Good recruiters check whether a staffing firm looks organised online before they join.
openers.hook: Only if they posted an internal job. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A staffing site with a careers page for your own team: {demo-link}

openers.line: You place workers in industrial parks across the county, but nothing online names them. A candidate who can't drive far wants to know which job sites are near home.
openers.hook: Look for job posts naming towns or parks. Name the cluster you see most.
openers.linkLine: Job sites by area on your recruiting page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Temp workers ask about pay day and how timesheets work before they take a staffing assignment. A page that answers it up front keeps them from going to the agency next door.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking about pay or hours on their job posts. If you see them, the angle is strong.
openers.linkLine: Pay day and timesheets explained for workers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Employers ask a staffing firm about workers' comp, liability coverage and any state agency licence before the first order. A page that shows what you hold answers it early.
openers.hook: Look for any licence or insurance mention on their listing or posts. Never claim one you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Coverage and licensing on one staffing page: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like most of your staffing orders come from a few plants. When one of them changes its HR manager, the new one may shop agencies from scratch.
openers.hook: Look for posts that mention one main employer or industry. Name the industry, not the company.
openers.linkLine: Where a new HR manager would find your agency: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a real recruiting win. A placement like that belongs on a page employers and candidates both see.
openers.hook: Pick their newest hiring or placement post and name it: the role, the shift and the type of employer.
openers.linkLine: That placement on your staffing site: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a real recruiting win.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found job posts on social media, but no jobs board a candidate could search and no way for an employer to send a headcount request. I put together a sample staffing site with both doors, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last note got buried under applications. Here's the sample staffing site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a searchable jobs board with apply-by-text, an employer headcount request, and pages for onboarding and pay day questions. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for staffing agencies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No surprise, recruiting days are long. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a jobs board candidates can search, an employer headcount request and a first-day checklist, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For an agency your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one direct-hire fee."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, after the morning dispatch?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: We post jobs on the big job boards already.
objections.handler: "Keep posting there. Those boards send candidates to your own jobs page, and an applicant who lands on your site stays your applicant instead of seeing a competitor's ad next to yours."

objections.objection: Our employers find us through relationships, not the web.
objections.handler: "They do. Their HR team still checks your staffing agency online before signing, and a night supervisor who needs workers wants a request form, not your cell."

objections.objection: We already have applicant tracking software.
objections.handler: "Good, the site sits in front of it. Jobs and applications flow to the system you already use, in whatever way it accepts them."

objections.objection: Candidates just walk in or text us.
objections.handler: "Keep both. The jobs board and apply-by-text catch the ones who look at night and never walk in."

objections.objection: We tried a website. It never brought in employers.
objections.handler: "Most staffing sites are built for candidates only. This one has a separate employer door with a headcount request and a recruiter call booking."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's two sites in one: a jobs board and an employer request. That's less than one direct-hire fee."

email.subject: Jobs board and employer page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for staffing agencies in {City}, and I made a sample site for {Business Name} with a jobs board and an employer request form. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} staffing demo down on Friday.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — warehouses around {City} start planning peak season staffing about now. Thought of you.

The staffing site with the jobs board and employer request is still here, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to less than one direct-hire fee; it's a staffing agency's easiest comparison.
Price it as two sites in one: the candidate jobs board and the employer door are each core.
Charge for bilingual applications separately; light industrial agencies feel that gap first.
Price industry pages one at a time: warehouse, manufacturing, clerical and skilled trades each read differently to an employer.
Never publish fill rates, placement counts or pay ranges the agency hasn't posted itself.
Keep monthly add-ons below one week's markup on a single temp worker.

lineItems.description: Max with filters by shift, location and role, apply-by-text, and jobs the recruiter can post from a phone.
Max with roles, headcount, shifts, PPE, site address and a recruiter call booking.
Max with the full application and job pages in two languages and a language toggle that remembers the choice.
Max when each page lists roles filled, shift options and the safety visit process for that industry.
Max with first-day checklist, document list, timesheet steps and a worker help request.

lineItems.item: Location pages by job site cluster (each)
lineItems.description: Max when each page lists open jobs in that area and directions to the agency office.

whatElseYouSell.name: Hiring event promotion
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each walk-in hiring day gets a landing page, a flyer and posts in two languages, all pointing to the staffing agency's jobs board."
whatElseYouSell.when: Before each hiring event, starting the month after launch.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with job posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New openings posted to your Google profile each week, so 'temp agency near me' shows an agency that's actively hiring."

whatElseYouSell.name: Employer outreach to plants and warehouses
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly note to HR and operations managers at nearby plants, offering a staffing call and the headcount request link."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the employer door is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Office photo and recruiter headshots
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Real photos of the office and each recruiter make the staffing site feel safe to a first-time applicant and credible to an HR manager."

whatElseYouSell.name: Worker and employer review requests
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Workers who finish an assignment and employers who convert a temp each get a short review request at the right moment."

whatElseYouSell.name: Peak season recruiting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before the autumn peak, a recruiting push for warehouse and seasonal shifts across social and local channels, all landing on the jobs board."

whatElseYouSell.name: Employer capability deck
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short deck for HR meetings: roles filled, safety visit process, onboarding steps and conversion terms, matching the staffing site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, before the next employer pitch.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plant you staff every week has a careers page nobody can find. Your recruiter can introduce me to their HR lead."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Employers trust the staffing partner who keeps their lines running.

withoutAI.route: Drug testing and background screening providers
withoutAI.whoPays: The screening provider, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The screening clinic your agency sends candidates to needs a booking page that agencies and employers can use."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Screening providers depend on agency volume and listen to them.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The forklift school that trains your candidates has a class schedule in a PDF. Your agency could send them students through a better page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Training schools and staffing firms share the same candidates.

withoutAI.whoPays: The supplier, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The boot and PPE shop where your workers gear up needs an order page for agencies and employers."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: PPE suppliers sell to every new placement.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The workforce board you partner with on hiring events has an events page that's hard to use on a phone. You can get me a meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Workforce boards fund job-seeker outreach and trust agencies that place people.

withoutAI.route: Shuttle and van transport for workers
withoutAI.whoPays: The transport company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The van service that drives your workers to the industrial park needs a schedule page riders can check."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Transport partners depend on staffing agencies for riders.

withAI.route: Job description writer for the employer's HR team
withAI.pitchLine: "HR managers describe the role in a sentence, and the assistant drafts a job description in plain language, ready for their careers page or the staffing order."
withAI.whyItWorks: Every employer hates writing job descriptions, and the agency client gets cleaner orders.

withAI.route: Appointment assistant for the screening clinic
withAI.pitchLine: "Candidates text to book a screening, and the assistant schedules them and tells the recruiting agency when it's done."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster screening means faster starts for the agency's placements.

withAI.route: Class enrolment assistant for the training school
withAI.pitchLine: "Prospective students ask about forklift class dates and costs, and the assistant answers from the school's schedule and books a seat."
withAI.whyItWorks: The staffing client sends students, and the school fills classes.

withAI.route: Reorder assistant for the PPE supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "Agencies tell the assistant next week's new starts and sites, and it drafts the boot, vest and glove order from the supplier's stock."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties every new placement to one supplier.

withAI.route: Job seeker intake assistant for the workforce board
withAI.pitchLine: "Job seekers answer a few questions by text, and the assistant points them to hiring events, training and partner staffing agencies."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards are funded for outreach, and the agency client is a partner.

withAI.route: Ride matching for the worker shuttle
withAI.pitchLine: "Workers text their address and shift, and the assistant drafts the van route for the next morning's staffing assignments."
withAI.whyItWorks: Better routes mean fewer no-shows for the agency.

softwareAI.name: Apply-by-text auto reply
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every candidate who texts about a job gets an instant reply with the application link and the staffing office's walk-in hours."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs a text-enabled number and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Shift confirmation texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The night before each assignment, workers get the site, start time, PPE list and who to ask for, and must reply to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the daily assignment list and worker phone numbers.

softwareAI.name: Candidate screener in two languages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants answer the recruiter's questions on shifts, transport and experience in their language, and the recruiter sees a ranked shortlist."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the recruiters' standard questions and must-haves per role. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Worker availability board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Who's available tomorrow, for which shifts, with which certificates and transport, on one board for the staffing desk."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the worker list and how they currently track availability.

softwareAI.name: Employer portal for orders and timesheets
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Employers place headcount orders, approve timesheets and rate workers from one portal, without calling the recruiting office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs employer logins and the timesheet process.

softwareAI.name: Job post writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Recruiters type the order details, and it drafts the job post in two languages with shift, pay as approved and requirements, ready for the jobs board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs past posts and the agency's rules for what to publish. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: No-show backfill alerts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a worker doesn't confirm a shift, the next available worker gets an offer by text before the staffing desk opens."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, with the availability board and shift confirmations.

softwareAI.name: Onboarding document checklist app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New hires upload their documents and complete orientation steps on a phone, and the recruiter sees what's missing before the first shift."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their onboarding steps, reviewed by their own adviser for document handling.

softwareAI.name: Employer call answering after hours
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers the agency line at night, takes the supervisor's headcount and shift, and texts the on-call recruiter a summary."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs on-call rules and the questions recruiters always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Placement and margin dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See hours billed, markup and fill time by employer, so the owner knows which staffing accounts are worth chasing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a few months of hours and bill rates.

softwareAI.name: Resume and application summariser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each application or resume becomes a short recruiter summary: shifts wanted, experience, transport and certificates, ready for the morning call list."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs sample applications and the recruiter's preferred summary format. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Redeploy reminders at assignment end
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A week before an assignment ends, the worker gets a note about upcoming jobs, so good temps stay with the agency."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs assignment end dates.

softwareAI.name: Worker feedback and rating log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Supervisors rate each temp after a shift, and the recruiter sees who to send back and who needs a different staffing assignment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, with the employer portal.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for worker pay and shift questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Workers ask 'when is pay day' or 'where do I report Monday' and get the staffing agency's approved answer instead of calling the office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the pay and onboarding pages and approved answers only. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Hiring event check-in app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Candidates check in at the hiring event on a tablet, start the application there, and recruiters see the line in order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before the next hiring event.

softwareAI.name: Employer proposal writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After an employer meeting, the recruiter's notes become a drafted staffing proposal with roles, shifts, onboarding steps and terms for approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past proposals and standard terms. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Certificate expiry tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Forklift cards and safety certificates for every worker, with alerts before they expire so the recruiting desk doesn't send someone unqualified."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs certificate records per worker.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for workers and employers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a worker or a plant manager posts about the staffing agency, a reply that fits who wrote it is ready for the owner to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bid notice watcher for public staffing contracts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Counties, schools and hospitals post temporary staffing contracts on public portals. It flags the ones in the agency's roles and region."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the portals they're registered on. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Referral bonus tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Workers refer friends with a personal link, and the agency tracks which referrals worked enough hours to earn the bonus the agency set."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the agency's referral rules and hours data.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Two-door staffing site as a monthly product
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Independent agencies need a jobs board and an employer door. I license the staffing site monthly with their jobs loaded."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first agency paid for the build and taught you the two-sided workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Member staffing firms get a jobs board, employer request and onboarding pages as a benefit of belonging."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want tools members use daily; one deal reaches many agencies.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each staffing office gets local jobs, local employer requests and recruiter pages under the brand. One build, every office."
"Partner staffing agencies post jobs to one regional portal that job seekers can search, with applications routed to each agency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Boards fund regional job access, and the client's jobs board is the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every staffing vendor posts confirmed workers, timesheets and ratings to one portal per site, so the operations manager stops reconciling spreadsheets."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large sites juggle several agencies; the client's employer portal shows you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The HR consultancy, per client site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "HR consultants set up careers pages for small employers. My recruiting template gives them a jobs board ready to brand."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Consultants sell the client; you sell the jobs board.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: First staffing firm in each metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built the two-door site for a staffing agency in {City}. I'll do it for one agency per metro, starting with whoever asks first."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity sells, and staffing firms rarely compete across metros.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Tenants in the park post openings to one hiring hub, with partner staffing agencies filling the temp roles."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Park owners sell easier hiring to tenants.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Graduates from short certificate programmes need first jobs. A page linking them to local staffing agencies and employers supports placement."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Colleges are measured on placement, and the client is a placement partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Temp cost estimator for employers, sponsored
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Employers estimate a temp worker's weekly cost from the sponsoring agency's own bill rates and send the staffing request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It never claims market rates, only the sponsor's.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The agency with an unfinished portal
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "An employer portal or jobs board left half-built is a short project for me. The timesheet and shift logic already runs for another staffing agency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Budget already spent; they need someone who knows temp staffing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Re-entry programmes need employers and staffing partners willing to hire. A jobs page connecting their participants to those openings helps both."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Grants fund job access, and the staffing client is the employer link.

upsellLadder.offer: Two-door staffing site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The staffing site and the care plan sit on one contract, so new jobs and new employer pages are a message to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: Applications through the jobs board outpace what recruiters can call back.
upsellLadder.line: "You're getting more applicants than calls in a day. Let the screener rank them so recruiting starts with the best fits."

upsellLadder.trigger: An employer complains about a day-one no-show.
upsellLadder.line: "That no-show cost your staffing desk trust with the plant. A confirm-by-text the night before catches it while there's time to backfill."

upsellLadder.offer: Employer outreach to plants and warehouses
upsellLadder.trigger: The employer headcount request brings in its first order.
upsellLadder.line: "An employer found the staffing request on their own. Let's put it in front of every plant near your office."

upsellLadder.trigger: Recruiters start missing fills because availability lives in texts and notebooks.
upsellLadder.line: "Your bench lives in each recruiter's phone. Put it on one board and fill orders faster."

upsellLadder.offer: Employer portal for orders and timesheets
upsellLadder.trigger: A large employer asks for online timesheet approval or a single view of their temps.
upsellLadder.line: "Give that employer a portal for orders and timesheets, and switching staffing agencies becomes a hassle they won't take on."

upsellLadder.trigger: The owner plans next year's accounts and asks which employers are worth it.
upsellLadder.line: "Before you chase new accounts, see which staffing clients actually make money."
